meta.projection_owner: Shared Governed State Applications & Reports Projection v1.3
meta.production_boundary: This registry is a read-only composite projection. Application approval/federation, agreement status/evidence, report artifact production, tenant entitlement, effective access, purpose, masking/RLS and assurance remain owned by their source authorities. Consumer and Auditor never mutate source authority through this catalog.

governance.authority_rule: Catalog visibility is not authorization. Every report open or federated application launch re-evaluates exact scope, entitlement, purpose, effective access, policy coverage, assurance and current source evidence.
governance.application_launch_rule: Federated launch requires current provider approval, current tenant/principal entitlement, current federated identity, sufficient assurance, exact organization scope, allowed purpose and all required effective dataset grants/policies.
governance.report_rule: Report artifacts are immutable, versioned governed snapshots. Open requires exact current report definition, exact definition-bound entitlement, exact tenant/institution/environment and organization scope, allowed purpose, sufficient assurance and every declared current effective dataset/policy prerequisite. Viewing a report never grants dataset/query/export access.
governance.audit_rule: Every eligibility review, report open and federated launch creates correlation/evidence metadata without exposing credentials or protected source payload.
governance.agreement_launch_rule: Applications declare exact required agreement ID/version contracts. Launch requires each current agreement projection to be Accepted, unexpired, evidence-backed, exact-version matched and not superseded without reacceptance.
governance.agreement_authority: Tenant Admin → Agreements & Participation current agreement projection; State Applications & Reports declares requirement only.
governance.report_definition_rule: Published report definitions are immutable and version/revision/hash bound. New definitions supersede rather than overwrite prior definitions; stale entitlements fail closed until explicitly rebound to the current definition contract.
